faqs.q: Cai Mep or Hai Phong — which port fits our plant?
faqs.a: The port at your end of the country. Cai Mep–Thi Vai serves Ho Chi Minh City, Binh Duong, Dong Nai, Ba Ria–Vung Tau and the Mekong Delta; Hai Phong serves Hanoi, Bac Ninh, Thai Nguyen and Quang Ninh. They are about 1,700 km apart by road, so landing at the wrong one costs a second freight bill rather than a few days. Name the delivery town at enquiry and we fix the port against it.

faqs.q: How many days should a Vietnamese buyer allow for a container from Jebel Ali?
faqs.a: Typically 18–24 days from dispatch for a full container, routed through the Strait of Malacca. Small mixed orders shipped LCL are consolidated with transhipment and take 24–32 days. Air freight from DXB to Ho Chi Minh City (SGN) or Hanoi (HAN) takes 3–5 days and suits a line that is down. Because the conformity file is light, freight is most of the timeline once the order is confirmed.

faqs.q: When does a Vietnamese order need a declaration of conformity?
faqs.a: Only where a specific line falls under a Vietnamese technical regulation. There is no blanket pre-shipment certification scheme for industrial hose, fittings and adapters, so most orders need no conformity document at all. Where a line is regulated, we prepare the declaration of conformity at origin before the vessel sails. Otherwise the file is the commercial invoice, the packing list, the Dubai Chamber attested Certificate of Origin and a clean customs declaration.

faqs.q: Which documents does a Vietnamese importer clear our goods with?
faqs.a: The importer’s customs declaration, filed through Vietnam Customs before the goods arrive, backed by our document set; import tax and VAT are settled at clearance. We supply what the declaration rests on: the commercial invoice and packing list, the Certificate of Origin attested by the Dubai Chamber, the declaration of conformity where a line is regulated, and material and test certificates where the order calls for them. All of it is prepared before the vessel sails.

faqs.q: Why does your quotation state an HS code against every line?
faqs.a: Because a mismatched classification is what slows clearance in Vietnam. The declaration itself is quick where the description on the invoice, the HS code and the importer’s declaration all agree; delay comes when the importer and the paperwork classify the same fitting differently. We state the classification line by line at quotation, so your broker declares exactly what we ship and the container is not queried at Cai Mep or Hai Phong.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to Da Nang, Dung Quat or Quy Nhon?
faqs.a: Yes. Da Nang takes a direct call on some services and a transhipment on others, so we quote it against the actual sailing rather than assuming one. For the Dung Quat refinery and steel complex in Quang Ngai, or for Quy Nhon, the road leg from Da Nang is usually the better answer than a separate port call. Give us the site and the receiving contact and we price the full route.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to factories in Binh Duong, Dong Nai or Bac Ninh?
faqs.a: Yes, on DAP terms to the factory gate. Binh Duong and Dong Nai are a road leg from Cai Mep–Thi Vai; Bac Ninh and the northern parks are a road leg from Hai Phong. The leg is priced at quotation rather than estimated. Tell us the industrial park, gate-entry rules and receiving hours, and the consignment is packed and labelled so the stores can book it straight in.

faqs.q: We are commissioning a new plant in Vietnam — how do we decide which hose assemblies to hold as spares?
faqs.a: Derive the list from the hydraulic schematic rather than waiting years for failure history. Pick out the assemblies that move with the machine, run near heat, bend on the tightest radius, or stop production when they fail, and hold those. We will do that reading from a drawing or a set of photographs, then crimp, pressure-test and tag each assembly in Dubai, so a repeat order is placed by tag reference.

faqs.q: Our fleet mixes Japanese, Korean and Chinese-built machines — can you match their hose ends?
faqs.a: Yes, by identifying each end from the part rather than the brand of machine. Mixed fleets in Vietnam commonly carry JIS, BSP, metric DIN and SAE or ORFS ends, sometimes on the same machine after earlier repairs. Send photographs and thread and seat measurements, or the failed assembly’s tag, and we confirm the end type at quotation before anything is crimped, so the assembly fits first time.

faqs.q: Can wellhead parts and flow iron for Cuu Long or Nam Con Son campaigns be quoted with our hose order?
faqs.a: Yes. We supply TechnipFMC, Cameron (SLB), SPM, Anson, Stream-Flo and WOM equipment, so wellhead components, valves and flow iron for Cuu Long and Nam Con Son basin campaigns can ship with hydraulic hose on one consignment. API 6A wellhead, API 16A BOP, API 16C choke and kill and API 7K drilling hose are available, with NACE MR0175 material documentation where the contract requires it. Name the supply base and campaign date and we plan the sailing back from it.

faqs.q: Can rigging hardware for a Hai Phong or Vung Tau yard come on the same container as hose?
faqs.a: Yes. Wire rope and chain slings, shackles, hooks and rigging hardware ship from Dubai marked with their working load limit and with the manufacturer’s test certificates the order calls for, on the same container as hydraulic parts. Any document a specific lifting line needs for import we confirm at quotation. Periodic inspection and the site lifting register stay with your yard’s appointed inspector.

faqs.q: Is hydraulic hose covered by the PS licence or the ICC mark?
faqs.a: Often not, but the part list decides. The PS licence, held by the manufacturer, and the ICC clearance, issued per shipment by the Bureau of Philippine Standards, are the two routes through the regulated-product scheme, and they apply to a defined list. A great deal of industrial hose and fittings sits outside it. Send the part list at quotation and we say which lines, if any, need clearance, rather than certifying everything to be safe.

faqs.q: What transit should a Luzon buyer plan on from Jebel Ali?
faqs.a: Typically 19–25 days from dispatch to Manila or Batangas for a full container, routed through the Strait of Malacca. Cargo for Cebu, Davao or Cagayan de Oro is transhipped onto a domestic sailing and takes 26–35 days in total. Air freight from DXB to Manila (MNL) takes 3–5 days. Any PS or ICC clearance is arranged before loading, so it does not add to the sailing.

faqs.q: When is Batangas a better port than Manila?
faqs.a: When Manila is congested or the delivery sits south of the capital. Manila suits most of Luzon, including Quezon City, Bulacan and Central Luzon. Batangas is closer to the Calabarzon estates in Laguna and Batangas and to the refinery and terminal sites on Batangas Bay. Name the delivery town at enquiry and we choose the port against it rather than defaulting to Manila.

faqs.q: What does the importer file with the Bureau of Customs, and what do you supply for it?
faqs.a: The importer lodges the import entry and internal revenue declaration through the Bureau of Customs before arrival. We prepare the documents it rests on: commercial invoice and packing list, a Certificate of Origin attested by the Dubai Chamber, the PS licence or ICC clearance where a line is listed, and material and test certificates where the order calls for them. Matching descriptions across all of them keep the entry from being queried.

faqs.q: Why is a Visayas or Mindanao delivery quoted separately from Manila?
faqs.a: Because the international sailing reaches Luzon and nowhere else. Cargo for Cebu, Iloilo, Davao or Cagayan de Oro waits for a domestic feeder, which adds a week or more however clean the paperwork is. Shipping to Manila and reconsigning later adds handling as well. Name the city where the goods are used, not the country, and the quotation states the real arrival date and the domestic leg.

faqs.q: Can you supply nickel mines in Surigao and the Caraga region?
faqs.a: Yes. Goods reach Mindanao on the domestic leg into Cagayan de Oro or Davao, and the move from the regional port to the mine site is quoted rather than estimated, because road conditions and the wet season change it. Laterite mining is wet, abrasive and dusty, so we specify hose covers, fittings and seals for abrasion and cycle life as well as pressure, and pack by machine or pit.

faqs.q: Which hose survives geothermal steam and H2S at Philippine plants?
faqs.a: Usually PTFE-lined or specific alloy metallic assemblies, chosen against the actual fluid analysis. Geothermal fluid at fields such as Tiwi, Makban and Leyte arrives hot, wet and carrying hydrogen sulphide; ordinary rubber constructions fail on temperature, and several stainless grades are vulnerable to sulphide stress cracking. Send the fluid composition, temperature and pressure, and the specification follows from it rather than from the word geothermal.

faqs.q: Do you supply valves and wellhead parts for Philippine gas and refinery work?
faqs.a: Yes. We supply TechnipFMC, Cameron (SLB), SPM, Anson, Stream-Flo and WOM equipment, so valves, flow iron and wellhead parts for the Batangas terminals, the Limay refinery or offshore gas work can ship with hydraulic hose. API 6A wellhead, API 16A BOP, API 16C choke and kill and API 7K drilling hose are available, with NACE MR0175 material documentation where the contract requires it. Ratings and certificates are confirmed per line at quotation.

faqs.q: Can a consignment go on from Manila to a Subic Bay Freeport or Clark address?
faqs.a: Yes, on DAP terms, by road from Manila. Subic Bay Freeport and Clark in Central Luzon are an overland leg from the port rather than a separate sailing, and that leg is priced at quotation. For shipyard and freeport deliveries, tell us the zone’s gate-entry and paperwork requirements at enquiry, so the truck is not held at the freeport gate.

faqs.q: Can wire rope slings and shackles for Subic Bay or Balamban yard work ship with our hydraulic order?
faqs.a: Yes. Wire rope and chain slings, shackles, hooks and lifting hardware ship from Dubai marked with their working load limit and with the manufacturer’s test certificates the order calls for, alongside hydraulic parts. Whether a lifting line falls on the PS or ICC list is checked from the part list at quotation. On-site inspection and the yard’s lifting records remain with your appointed inspector.

faqs.q: Does air freight into Manila help a mine or plant in the Visayas or Mindanao?
faqs.a: Sometimes, for a line that is down. Air takes 3–5 days from DXB to Manila against 19–25 days by sea, but the onward move to an outer island still has to be booked, and it does not run faster because the goods arrived by air. For a planned shutdown, sea freight planned back from the outage date is usually the better answer.

faqs.q: Why do you publish a 12–16 day sea leg but no door-to-door time for Myanmar?
faqs.a: Because the two are different questions. Jebel Ali to Thilawa is 12–16 days by sea, among the shorter lanes east of the Gulf and comparable with Malaysia. A door-to-door time would be a promise about corridors no supplier controls: the country has been in armed conflict since 2021, and which inland routes operate changes. So onward routing is confirmed per consignment, against what is actually running.

faqs.q: Who and what do you check before quoting a Myanmar buyer?
faqs.a: The buyer, the ultimate recipient, the end use and the installation site, all checked before we quote rather than after an order is taken. We screen this way because the measures that apply to Myanmar are drawn around particular organisations and activities rather than the country as a whole. Where we cannot satisfy ourselves, we decline plainly.

faqs.q: Which details let you screen a Myanmar enquiry quickly?
faqs.a: The end user, the installation site and the application, alongside the part list. Restrictions here turn on the identity of the ultimate recipient and the use of the equipment, so an enquiry that names all three can be assessed quickly. One that leaves them out cannot be assessed at all, and chasing the details afterwards costs time on both sides. Include the importer’s details as the consignee.

faqs.q: Will you tell us if you cannot supply an order?
faqs.a: Yes, clearly and at the screening stage. Where an enquiry falls outside what we are able to supply, we say so at that point rather than letting it lapse into silence or quoting first and withdrawing later. That applies to the counterparty, the end use and the installation site alike, and it is why screening comes before pricing on this lane.

faqs.q: Do containers discharge at Thilawa or in Yangon?
faqs.a: Our default sea routing is Jebel Ali to Thilawa, the terminal area downriver of Yangon, with Yangon named as an alternative port of entry where the sailing serves it. Either way the sea leg is 12–16 days. We confirm the discharge port with the routing at quotation, after screening has cleared, and quote CIF Yangon where that is the agreed basis.

faqs.q: Will you quote delivery to Mandalay or a site away from Yangon?
faqs.a: Only where a route can genuinely be committed. We quote DAP where that is true and to the quay where it is not, and the quotation says which rather than implying a door delivery we cannot stand behind. Onward routing is confirmed against the corridors actually operating at the time, not a published map, and screening of the recipient and site comes first.

faqs.q: Which licence must the Myanmar consignee hold?
faqs.a: An import licence held by the consignee, with confirmation that it covers the goods on the invoice. Beyond that the file is the customs declaration raised by the importer, the commercial invoice and packing list, and a Certificate of Origin attested by the Dubai Chamber. We prepare our documents only after counterparty and end-use screening has cleared, and before the vessel sails.

faqs.q: What does cargo cover on a Thilawa consignment actually insure?
faqs.a: Whatever scope we state in the quotation, because cover is arranged per consignment, priced in, and its scope written down before you accept. Because the inland leg varies with routing and conditions, what is insured on the sea leg and what is insured beyond the quay can differ, and we spell that out rather than leaving it to be discovered after a claim. Ask at enquiry if you need a particular scope of cover.

faqs.q: Why do you suggest landing several Myanmar orders as one consignment?
faqs.a: Because on a lane where the sea leg is reliable and the inland leg is not, one consignment landed and cleared together is far easier to move onward than several arriving separately, each needing its own routing. Each order still goes through screening, but a consolidated enquiry can be screened and routed once, which shortens the overall timeline.

faqs.q: Can an urgent part be flown to Yangon instead of waiting for a sailing?
faqs.a: Sometimes: air freight is offered only where the routing permits, and it is quoted per consignment rather than published. It makes sense for a small, urgent item where the sea leg would leave a line down. Screening applies exactly as it does to sea freight, so an air shipment cannot skip the counterparty and end-use checks, and onward delivery from the airport is confirmed in the same way as from the port.

faqs.q: If a hose fails on a Yangon site, what do you need to replace it?
faqs.a: The bore, thread, working pressure and length between fitting faces, or photographs of the failed assembly, plus the end user and site for screening. Once screening clears, assemblies are crimped in Dubai, pressure-tested and tagged with hose, fitting and test date, then packed as finished items, so nothing has to be made up after an uncertain inland move, and a repeat order can be placed by tag reference.

faqs.q: What is the full transit from Dubai to Cambodia by each route?
faqs.a: By sea to Sihanoukville, transhipped, typically 24–32 days from dispatch. By sea to Cai Mep, then road through the Bavet border to Phnom Penh, typically 22–28 days. By air from DXB to Phnom Penh (PNH), 4–6 days, for a line that is down. The quotation names the route chosen and the reason, so you can see why one was preferred for that order.

faqs.q: Is there a Cambodian equivalent of TISI or SNI for hydraulic hose?

That leaves the routing, not the paperwork, as the decision that sets the arrival date.

faqs.q: What is a Cambodian import declaration filed against?
faqs.a: Our commercial invoice and packing list, lodged by the importer through the General Department of Customs before the goods arrive. It is supported by the Dubai Chamber attested Certificate of Origin, and material and test certificates where the order calls for them. On the overland routing the Vietnamese transit documents must match the same invoice line for line, so we prepare the whole set together.

faqs.q: What must be settled before a container leaves Cai Mep for Bavet?
faqs.a: The delivery town and confirmation that you can clear at Bavet. If the overland routing is the faster one, the Vietnamese transit documents are raised by the forwarder at Cai Mep and have to be ready before the container leaves the port. Give us both at enquiry and the transit file is arranged alongside the order rather than after the vessel arrives in Vietnam.

faqs.q: How long is the road leg from Cai Mep to Phnom Penh?
faqs.a: About a day on the road once the goods are cleared, Ho Chi Minh City to Phnom Penh. The variable is the Bavet crossing rather than the distance: a file that matches line for line moves; one that does not waits. That is why we quote the leg as part of the route, rather than adding an estimate to the sea time.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to factories in the Phnom Penh or Sihanoukville special economic zones?
faqs.a: Yes, on DAP terms to the factory gate. Phnom Penh zones are usually reached via Cai Mep and Bavet, Sihanoukville zones from the port itself, and either leg is priced at quotation rather than estimated. Tell us the zone, the factory’s receiving hours and any gate-entry paperwork, and we pack and label the consignment so it can be booked straight into stores.

faqs.q: Our excavator came to Cambodia second-hand — should we order from the parts book?
faqs.a: No, measure what is actually fitted. A machine that has passed through several owners often carries substituted fittings, rerouted hoses or adapted ports, so the parts book describes a machine that no longer exists. Send dimensions or photographs of the part you are replacing, with the thread, seat and length between fitting faces. If they disagree with the manual we tell you, and the assembly is crimped and pressure-tested in Dubai.

faqs.q: Can you supply kiln and crusher hydraulics for Kampot cement plants?
faqs.a: Yes. Kampot is a short road leg from Sihanoukville, and delivery to the plant on DAP terms is priced at quotation. Kiln, crusher and loader hydraulics in cement and limestone quarry service run hot, dusty and continuous, so we specify hose cover, fittings and seals for abrasion, heat and cycle life as well as pressure, and supply the same construction on every reorder.

faqs.q: Laem Chabang is three weeks from Jebel Ali — why is Vientiane closer to five?

faqs.q: Is anything about the product itself certified before goods enter Laos?
faqs.a: No. Laos has no general pre-shipment conformity scheme for industrial hose and fittings, so nothing about the product needs certifying before it moves. faqs.q: Who prepares the Thai transit declaration and the Lao customs declaration?
faqs.a: The forwarder raises the Thai transit declaration at Laem Chabang for the bonded move; the importer lodges the Lao declaration through Lao Customs before the goods reach the border. faqs.q: Why does the Thanaleng border, not the sailing, set the arrival date?
faqs.a: Because a mismatch stops the truck at the border rather than at either customs office, and the border keeps its own hours. A file that is short one document, or where the Thai and Lao paperwork disagree on a line, waits for the next working day. Everything that can be planned on this lane is on the paperwork side, so we finish it before the vessel sails.

faqs.q: Should goods for Savannakhet or Pakse come through Thailand or Vietnam?

For Savannakhet, Pakse and the southern provinces, the east–west corridor from Da Nang can beat coming south from Vientiane after the Laem Chabang route; the Da Nang routing typically runs 30–40 days. We compare both against the actual sailings and the delivery site, and the quotation says which route was chosen and why.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to mine sites around Sepon and in the southern provinces?

faqs.q: Which seals and hose suit dam gates and spillway actuators in Laos?

faqs.q: Can you deliver past the border to a Vientiane site?

The container moves under Thai bond from Laem Chabang, crosses at Thanaleng and is delivered onward, with the road leg priced at quotation rather than estimated. Tell us the site, receiving hours and any zone entry paperwork, and the consignment is labelled to match the Lao declaration.

faqs.q: When should a Lao site fly a part in rather than wait for the road?

faqs.q: Can lifting gear for a Lao dam or road project travel on the same transit file as hydraulic parts?

faqs.q: Atlantic or Pacific — which lane will our Canadian shipment take?

faqs.q: Can cargo go through Halifax or Prince Rupert instead of Montreal or Vancouver?
faqs.a: Yes, where the delivery suits it. Halifax sits on the Atlantic routing through Suez, and Prince Rupert is a Pacific gateway on the Malacca side. faqs.q: We build packages in Alberta for Gulf and Caspian contracts — can you supply the destination-standard parts?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is most of our Canadian trade. A package bound for the Gulf, Africa or the Caspian has to be plumbed to that market’s standard — GOST couplings, DIN bite-type fittings, BSP threads — which is stock for us. faqs.q: Our equipment is deployed in Africa or Central Asia — can spares go there direct from Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is usually cheaper than routing them through Canada. A mine or rig in Africa or Central Asia is far closer to Jebel Ali than to Montreal or Vancouver. faqs.q: What minimum temperature should we give you for hose working an Alberta or Saskatchewan winter?
faqs.a: The lowest ambient the hose will see while idle and while being moved, not just while running. That number, rather than the working pressure, decides the compound: a standard compound stiffens well above prairie winter temperatures, while low-temperature constructions stay flexible. We specify low-temperature material wherever an assembly is exposed outdoors through the winter.

faqs.q: Why does a frozen hose fail hours after start-up rather than straight away?
faqs.a: Because the damage happens when it is bent cold. Below its rated temperature an elastomer behaves like plastic, so flexing a hose that sat outside overnight can crack the tube without marking the cover. The leak appears later, once the machine warms up and pressurises. Low-temperature constructions avoid that, which makes it a specification choice rather than a quality one.

faqs.q: How long is the sea voyage from Jebel Ali to Colón, and when does air make sense?

faqs.q: What is the Colón Free Zone and does it help us?
faqs.a: It lets goods be landed, stored and re-dispatched without entering Panamanian customs territory. If your cargo is staying in Panama it makes no difference to you. If you are staging stock for Central America or the northern South American coast, it is the reason to route through Colón at all — and the Free Zone documentation is raised by the Zone operator on arrival, so we need to know before we ship.

faqs.q: Can you ship stock into the Colón Free Zone for onward dispatch to Central America?

Tell us at quotation, because the file differs from the outset: goods held in the Zone can be re-dispatched onward on their own documentation, while goods imported and then re-exported have paid for a round trip through the customs system they did not need. Converting one into the other after arrival is possible, and expensive.

faqs.q: Should our cargo be routed to Colón or to Balboa?
faqs.a: Colón for Atlantic-side cargo and the Free Zone; Balboa for the Pacific side and Panama City. The two are a short move apart across the isthmus, but the file is raised against one of them, so name the delivery point at quotation. Manzanillo and Cristóbal sit on the Colón side, and DAP to your site is quoted as a single price including the road leg.

So we specify impulse-rated construction and correct crimp retention rather than matching the part number alone. Send the duty cycle with the specification and we quote against both.

faqs.q: How many weeks should a Jamaican plant allow for a sea shipment from Dubai?
faqs.a: Typically 30–38 days by sea from dispatch for a full container from Jebel Ali through Suez and across the Atlantic to Kingston. LCL runs 36–48 days, consolidated and transhipped, which suits small mixed orders rather than an outage date. Air freight from DXB to Kingston takes 4–7 days with connections when a line is down and the plant cannot wait.

faqs.q: Can you supply hose for the caustic and slurry circuits of an alumina refinery?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the reason most Jamaican enquiries reach us. Caustic liquor, heat and abrasive slurry in one circuit will destroy a general-purpose hose in weeks — a compound chosen for hydraulic oil is the wrong compound there. Tell us the concentration, the temperature and where in the circuit the assembly sits, and we specify against it and say plainly where a catalogue item is unsuitable.

faqs.q: Why should aluminium quick-couplings be kept out of Bayer-process lines?
faqs.a: Because aluminium is attacked by caustic outright, and it turns up in fittings and quick-couplings where nobody expected chemistry to matter. Hot caustic is also far more aggressive than the ambient figure a compatibility table gives. Give us the sodium hydroxide concentration and the operating temperature, not just the chemical name, and we specify tube, cover and end fittings against all three.

faqs.q: Our cargo is going through Kingston — will it be imported or transhipped?
faqs.a: That depends on where it is going, and it is worth saying which at quotation. Kingston transhipes a great deal that never enters Jamaica. If your goods are staying, the importer raises the customs declaration through Jamaica Customs before arrival; if they are staging onward, the file is documented that way from the outset rather than imported and re-exported.

faqs.q: Is a conformity certificate required to import industrial hose into Jamaica?
faqs.a: No — there is no blanket pre-shipment conformity scheme for industrial hose and fittings. The file is the customs declaration raised by the importer through Jamaica Customs, the invoice and packing list, the Dubai Chamber attested certificate of origin and the bill of lading or air waybill. For caustic and slurry duty we add a compatibility statement, and material and test certificates where the plant specification calls for them.

faqs.q: Can you deliver DAP to the refineries in Clarendon and at Ewarton?
faqs.a: Yes, on DAP terms to the plant gate — the Clarendon refinery, Ewarton in St Catherine, or the Nain site in St Elizabeth. The road leg from Kingston, or from Port Esquivel where the berth suits, is priced with the order rather than estimated. Give us the gate and the receiving contact with the enquiry and both go on the file before dispatch.

faqs.q: Why source alumina-plant hose from Dubai rather than Florida?
faqs.a: For a standard item, Florida is closer and often the right answer. What we hold is the caustic and slurry specification as stock rather than as a special order, and on a plant with a shutdown calendar that is worth more than the freight difference. A consignment planned against the outage lands with the compound, couplings and documents settled.

faqs.q: Should we batch our orders around the refinery shutdown calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. On a five-week lane, one consolidated consignment planned against the shutdown calendar lands far better than several small ones ordered as items fail: compound and coupling choices are settled once, documents are raised once, and the assemblies arrive before the outage rather than during it. Send the outage date with the line list and we work back from it.

faqs.q: Which Jamaican ports can you ship to besides Kingston?
faqs.a: Kingston is the default port of entry, with Port Esquivel and Montego Bay used where the berth suits the delivery. Port Esquivel sits close to the St Catherine and Clarendon bauxite and alumina operations; Montego Bay serves the north-west. Whichever port is chosen, the road leg to site is priced with the order on DAP terms, and the file is raised against that port.

faqs.q: Can you match the fittings on bauxite haul trucks and loaders exactly?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the existing fitting identification — thread form, seat angle and sealing method — or the machine model, and we match it, whether JIC, ORFS, BSP or metric, rather than substituting a near-equivalent. Hose is supplied to SAE J517, EN 853/856 or ISO 18752 constructions as the machine requires, and abrasion-resistant covers are worth specifying where lines rub in the bauxite pits.

faqs.q: Which flexible connections should we specify for seismic movement in Chilean plants?
faqs.a: Flexible sections wherever a line crosses between independently mounted equipment, installed with slack and a bend radius that lets them move. Rigid pipework transmits ground movement straight to a flange, which is where fractures appear after an earthquake. A hose pulled tight between two fixed points behaves like a rigid member with a weaker wall. Where temperature or media rule out rubber, braided metallic hose does the same job.
